lines.text: Unit 02Spread of Islam
Architecture
One of the major architectural activities of the Abbasid caliphs was building large new
cities. The most important of these cities was Baghdad. About 2.7 kilometres, Baghdad
was surrounded by mud-brick walls. Another city wasal-Rafiqa that was constructed by
al-Mansur. It was protected by a wall, nearly 5 kilometres.
City of Samaraa was located around 125 kilometres North of Baghdad. This city served as
capital of the Abbasids for a brief period during ninth century AD. The city was
constructed by Mu'tasim, the son of Haroon-ur-Rashid.
In addition to cities, some grand Masjids were also built during that period. Caliph
al-Moutawakel build a huge Masjid in Samaraa with total area of 41 acres.For many
centuries it was the largest masjid in the world.
Another marvel of Abbasid architecture is Ibn Talun Masjid in Cairo. It was built by Ibn
Talunwhowasgovernorof EgyptandSyria in869AD.
Abbasid Palace of Ukhaider is located roughly 5o km south of Karbala, Iraq. It is a large,
rectangular fortress erected in 775 AD with a unique defensive style.
DeclineofAbbasidCaliphate
The periods of Caliphs Mansur, Mehdi, Harun Rashid, Ma'mun Rashid, and Mu'tasim is
considered as“golden era"of theAbbasids.Foundations of Islamic civilizations were laid
mostly during this period.The period of declinethat startedin9th centurycontinueduntil
collapse of Abbasids in 1258 AD.There were many factors behind this decline'that include
both internal as well as external factors.Some of the importantfactors are as under:
1.Differencesamongvarious groups caused continuous unrest.Ethnic,political and
regional disputes weakened the state. As the state expanded significantly, Arabs, Persians,
Syrians, Berber, Christians, Jewish and Turks had open differences with each other that
caused continuous conspiraciesagainsttherulers.
2. Luxurious lifestyle of the rulersdestroyed their military virtues. Reign of early
Abbasids is considered as golden period of the caliphate. However,this was also the time
when extravagance was at its peak. Moreover, even in later years of decline, the rulers
were more indulged in luxuries and comforts.
3. Disintegration of different areas of caliphate started and several autonomous
dynasties appeared. The first such autonomous state was the Emirate of Cordoba where
Umayyadsbecame sovereign rulers in756AD.
